newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Israel, PLO to restore calm after riots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Israel, PLO to restore calm after riots.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday urged all sides to quickly restore calm after bloody rioting in the West Bank left at least one Palestinian dead.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns advised Israel and the Palestinians to negotiate on existing differences and avoid raising "new issues." The riots were sparked by Israel's decision to open a tunnel near a holy Islamic site.
"The United States firmly believes that neither Israel nor the Palestinians should create other issues that can make the situation more difficult," Burns told reporters.
Israeli soldiers shot and killed at least one Palestinian, wounded more than 200 and exchanged fire with Yasser Arafat's police in the bloodiest clashes in the West Bank in two years.
The fighting began after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu decided to open a tunnel in Jerusalem near the Dome of the Rock and al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.

Burns said U.S. officials were in constant touch, meaning "several phone calls an hour" with the region. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, in New York for a U.N. General Assembly session, was being kept informed, he said.
"The United States urges all sides to move quickly to restore calm in Israel, Gaza and the West Bank, to avoid further violence and to show and exercise restraint," he said.

"We believe that the parties to the Oslo accords -- Israel and the Palestinian Authority -- have agreed that Jerusalem issues are final status issues and should be discussed between them in a calm and peaceful setting."

Wednesday's clashes outside the PLO-ruled enclave of Ramallah were reminiscent of the 1987-1993 Palestinian uprising, or intifada, against Israel -- only now there are nearly 30,000 armed Palestinian police in self-rule areas.
Israeli troops fired live ammunition and rubber bullets when they came under a hail of stones and bottles at the crossing to the Ramallah enclave, north of Jerusalem, witnesses said.
